target_customer: Air travelers, especially premium and business travelers, who book airport meet and greet, fast track and concierge escorts
problem: Travelers lose hours at arrival, customs, security and connections, and escort services are fragmented across hundreds of independent local operators.
business_model: Marketplace and booking aggregator taking a margin on airport escort and fast track services

founders.name: Justin Vencel
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists him as Founder and CTO with no background. Blacklane's release quotes a different person, Blaine Vess, as founder and CEO; this was seen only in a search snippet, so the founding team is unresolved.

technical_complexity.rationale: A booking website and operations layer over local escort providers; the hard part was supplier coverage and operations, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: TechCrunch described a fragmented market of independent escort operators that Solve aggregated; supplier agreements were non-exclusive and the booking layer was easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Blacklane bought Solve in October 2017, three months after launch coverage, to add airport concierge to its chauffeur service, and relaunched it as Blacklane PASS in 2018.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in July 2017 noted over 500 airports with escort providers and a fragmented supply side; no demand or revenue figures were found.

branding.domain_note: solve.com is the listed website but returned 404 when fetched; domain history not found.

rebrands.why: Blacklane rebuilt and relaunched the service under its own brand after the acquisition, per trade coverage.

brand_strength.rationale: Only a few months of public life, one TechCrunch article, and the name was retired into Blacklane PASS. A generic one-word name is also hard to search for.

outcome_analysis: Solve joined YC in Summer 2017 as a two person team aggregating airport escort providers and was acquired by Blacklane in October 2017, only a few months after launch coverage. Price and terms were not disclosed and the brand was rebuilt as Blacklane PASS, so this looks like a fast, small strategic exit rather than proof of traction; the evidence for traction is thin.
notes: Unverified: CB Insights lists about $120K raised from Blacklane, YC and Taurus Ventures (single aggregator); a Signalbase page claims $55M, which looks wrong. Neither is recorded as a round. The Blacklane press release URL returned 404 on fetch; its date (2017-10-11) comes from search results and tech.eu. Competitor search found only undated or later providers (Fasttrack.aero, airssist), so the list is empty. The failure factor acquihire_soft_landing is an inference from the speed and thin product history, not a source statement.
